newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mixed on Monday after a quiet session with little cash trade, dealers said.

The French Left's election win did not have much effect on guilder debt. Dealers said the victory had been anticipated, but they added market players needed some reassurance on the chances for economic and monetary union (EMU) to start on time.
"Investors await remarks from the new French government on the direction of EMU and they also expect the quarrel in Germany on the revaluation of its gold reserves to continue," said one dealer.
The German government was deeply divided today over Finance Minister Waigel's plans to fill the budget deficit by revaluing the nation's gold reserves.
"This fight will probably continue for some more time," said one dealer. He said this would depress sentiment in the bond market.

Another dealer said he expected the yield on the February 2007 bond to rise to 6.00 percent from the current level of 5.79 percent if the quarrel continued as it would create more uncertainty about the future of EMU.
